plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and prized for its early spring blooms, which often appear while frost and snow linger.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in Japan as heralds of spring, and the fruit is pickled to make umeboshi and steeped to make umeshu liqueur.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with a distinctive trumpet-shaped corona surrounded by pale outer petals. It carpets woodlands and meadows in early spring, and many cultivated daffodil varieties descend from it.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (late February to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: The daffodil is the national flower of Wales and is traditionally worn on St. David's Day, March 1.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree or large shrub with feathery foliage and fluffy, ball-shaped flower clusters. In Australia it blooms from late winter into spring, making bright splashes of gold in the bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October in Australia, with some variation by region and species)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring there.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes through snow and thrives in woodlands, gardens, and churchyards.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Europe from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.
